summary.text: A preterm male infant born vaginally at 30 weeks of gestation weighed 1200 g with Apgar scores of 6 and 8, needed minimal resuscitation and was transferred to neonatal intensive care. His mother had a 2-month coma of unknown etiology in the third trimester and was diagnosed with smear-positive pulmonary TB at 1 week postpartum.

At 3 weeks he presented with cervical lymphadenopathy and failure to thrive and was treated for sepsis with ceftriaxone without clinical improvement. The lymphadenopathy fistulized near the pinna of the ear at 7 weeks, with a normal ear examination, and respiratory distress with tachypnea and oxygen dependency led to a 12-day ICU admission.

On admission to the center he weighed 1700 g. Chest X-ray was normal, lymph node ultrasound showed hypoechoic masses with central necrosis, node biopsy showed caseating granulomas with Langhans giant cells, GeneXpert MTB on lymph node aspirate was positive, and blood and CSF cultures were negative for bacterial pathogens; the HIV test was negative. Congenital tuberculous lymphadenitis was diagnosed by Cantwell criteria.

Antitubercular therapy with isoniazid, rifampicin and pyrazinamide was started at 4 months of life, without ethambutol, for a planned 6-month course. Lymphadenopathy resolved gradually over 8 weeks of treatment with no hepatotoxicity, and at 3 months of treatment he showed significant clinical improvement with resolved respiratory distress.

article_limitations: Ultrasound and histopathology images are not included in the article; only Figure 1 (clinical photograph) is available.
The case narrative states that ultrasound measures, abdominal imaging, laboratory ranges, oxygen saturations and heart rate at key points were not available.

Mother is not a separate roster patient; her history is recorded with subject mother. The source says her own records were not accessed and her history came from a referral note after interviewing the caregiver.
